mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces discount rates applied to future corporate earnings, lowering the present value of expected cash flows and thus driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar rate hike events, or the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4% during the target horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: In 70% of similar labor market tightening events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.1), or the correlation between PAYEMS acceleration and SPX 60-day return is <0.2.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future earnings and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate > 0.3% for 3 months
failure_condition: Over 50 similar demand acceleration events, the 5-day forward return is negative on average (mean < 0), or the 5-day return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -2% for two consecutive months suggests weakening supply conditions, prompting market participants to price in higher future inflation and slower growth, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 60% of historical supply contraction episodes, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (mean > 0), or the correlation between INDPRO contraction and negative SPX 20-day return is < -0.3.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5%, it triggers a shift in risk aversion as markets anticipate higher future policy rates, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During 10 similar FEDFUNDS hikes, the 20-day forward return is on average positive (mean > 0), or the cross-asset correlation between FEDFUNDS spike and SPX decline is < -0.4.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a rise in job openings (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which elevates wage growth expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 while UNRATE falls by >0.1 percentage points for 2 months
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor market tightness events, the 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.1), or the 60-day return is negatively correlated with the strength of the labor signal (r < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in personal consumption (CPIAUCSL) of over 0.5% for three months suggests waning demand momentum, which reduces growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During 40 historical demand cooling episodes, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in >75% of cases, or the 20-day return is positively correlated with CPIAUCSL deceleration (r > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) shows a double-digit monthly decline followed by a rebound of less than 2% in the subsequent month, it signals a supply shock with incomplete recovery, which increases perceived risk and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO drops by >10% in a month, then rebounds by <2% in the next month
failure_condition: In 30 historical partial supply disruptions, the 60-day forward return is on average non-negative (mean >= 0), or the 60-day return is not significantly different from baseline (p > 0.05).
